errors.text: The central structural mediator is misidentified as a percolating/coarsening B2 network rather than enhanced L12 ordering in FCC domains coupled to jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries.
The proposed 400-600°C aging range omits the approximately 750°C ductility-recovery condition and does not define the requested boundaries of <550°C, 550-750°C, and >750°C.

Recovery is attributed to thermal activation over lattice friction even though aging and mechanical testing temperatures may differ; the target recovery instead involves reduced ordering and ductile transition zones at phase boundaries.

The cited evidence does not establish the requested ordered-domain dislocation mechanism involving elevated antiphase-boundary energy, restricted cross-slip, and planar slip. Evidence E3 and E4 concerns different systems and mechanisms, while E1 suggests that a continuous network can impede cracks rather than cause embrittlement.

The proposed falsification rule tests the new percolation hypothesis but does not directly falsify classical grain-boundary embrittlement by demonstrating the absence of grain-boundary impurity segregation and locating pile-ups or crack initiation at jagged phase-boundary tips.
